### Token-deduplicated EP dispatch (`ring_dedup`): 1.580 s and 14.31% MFU with `save_moe`, -8.7% against ring

Commit: 91286fc (local; `ring_dedup` backend in b31085d, merged onto the gather-combine base 67ca557) · GPU: MI350X ×8 · Jobs: 454021 (`ring_dedup`), 454012 (ring baseline)

PR: #9880 (draft, merge after #9860). `--pooled-transport-capacity-factor` comes from #9852.

```bash
JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ENABLE_XLA_CACHES=none RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.90 \
  sbatch --export=ALL -N1 -p mi3508x -t 45 -o "logs/%x-%j.out" experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/run_gpu.sh \
  experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py --size full --steps 20 --expert-axis 8 --watch-interval 0 \
  --compilation-cache-dir <fresh private dir> --batch-size 64 --attention gpu_pallas_triton_flash \
  --moe-impl ring_dedup --pooled-transport-capacity-factor 1.1 --remat-mode save_moe
```

| Step | Tokens/s | MFU | Peak mem |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.580 s | 165,900 | 14.31% | 206.5 GiB |

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- **What it does.** `ring` all-gathers every token to all 8 GPUs and reduce-scatters a full-size output, but with top-4 of 256 experts a token reaches only 3.3 GPUs on average. `ring_dedup` (new module `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring_dedup.py`) sends each token once to each GPU that owns one of its experts, through a fixed-capacity `all_to_all`, plus a small `all_to_all` of per-row combine weights and local expert ids. The expert side keeps ring's capacity rule, grouped layout and Triton `ragged_dot`, sums each token's local expert outputs in f32 and returns one row per token. All hidden-width movement is a gather (ring's `_dispatch_rows`/`_combine_rows`), so there are no scatter-adds in either pass.
- **Sender capacity** is `--pooled-transport-capacity-factor` times the expected distinct tokens per destination under uniform routing (0.416 × 32,768 per GPU). At 1.1 it sends 537 MB per collective per GPU, against 1,174 MB for ring's all-gather or reduce-scatter (46%), and drops no tokens at the sender in these runs.
- **A/B, batch 64, flash attention, fresh compile cache per job, `JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ENABLE_XLA_CACHES=none`, median of steps 2-19:**

  | Base | Remat | ring | `ring_dedup` | Jobs |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | merged (gather combine + Triton routing top-k) | recompute_all | 1.798 s, 12.57% | 1.688 s, 13.40% (-6.1%) | 454022, 454026 |
  | merged | save_moe | 1.730 s, 13.07% | 1.580 s, 14.31% (-8.7%) | 454012, 454021 |
  | before the gather combine | recompute_all | 1.865 s, 12.13% | 1.735 s, 13.03% (-7.0%) | 453921, 453922 |
  | before the gather combine | save_moe | 1.842 s, 12.28% | 1.637 s, 13.81% (-11.1%) | 453960, 453968 |

  The two changes stack partly. With `save_moe`, the gather combine alone saves 112 ms, `ring_dedup` alone 205 ms, both together 262 ms. Peak memory changes by at most 0.7 GiB. Step-19 loss is within 8e-4 of ring in every pair. The drop rate is 1.00% vs 0.99% (`recompute_all`) and 1.12% vs 0.93% (`save_moe`).
- **Numerics.** f32 CPU unit tests on 8 shards match ring and a dense reference to 1e-5 in value and in gradients for x, combine weights and both expert weights, including a forced sender-drop case. At full shapes in bf16 on MI350X, one layer differs from ring by 0.2-0.5% relative in value and gradients. That comes from ring's bf16 summation; `ring_dedup` sums in f32.
- **Profile (steps 10-12, GPU 0, ms per profiled step, ring vs `ring_dedup`, both before the gather combine).** `recompute_all`: large EP collectives take 481 vs 311, exposed collective time is 357 vs 288, and MoE dispatch/combine kernels take 150 vs 42. `save_moe`: 386 vs 211, 402 vs 266, and 147 vs 40. Each large `all_to_all` takes 1.6-2.7 ms, against 3.3-4.2 ms for ring's collectives.
- **What is still exposed:** the forward return and backward dy `all_to_all`s are synchronous (about 60 ms each per step), and the small metadata `all_to_all`s take 0.8-0.9 ms per call under `save_moe`, where they queue behind the large transfers.
- The latency-hiding scheduler gave 1.594 s vs 1.637 s before the merge, but 1.591 s vs 1.580 s after it (job 454027), so leave it off.
- One run (454010) hit the step-5 GPU-7 out-of-memory on a 96.6 GiB allocation, the same failure seen at batch 96 in job 453660, and hung. The retry (454021) ran clean. Since diagnosed as allocator fragmentation around the step's temp buffer and fixed by `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false` (#9901).
- **Follow-ups:** packing the metadata into the activation rows and chunking the expert MLP were tried and did not help; see the next comment. Not tested on TPU or NVIDIA.

</details>

### One gradient all-reduce per weight after the layer scan: works, keeps gradients, no speedup on MI350X

Commit: bd8e11a · GPU: MI350X ×8 · Job: 453915 (on 60b253d), 454011 (on 67ca557)

```bash
RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.90 JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ENABLE_XLA_CACHES=none sbatch --export=ALL -N1 -p mi3508x -t 45 -o "logs/%x-%j.out" experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/run_gpu.sh experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py --size full --steps 20 --expert-axis 8 --watch-interval 0 --compilation-cache-dir <fresh private dir> --batch-size 64 --attention gpu_pallas_triton_flash --remat-mode <recompute_all|save_moe>
```

| Base | Remat | Variant | Step | Tokens/s | MFU | Peak mem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60b253d | recompute_all | baseline | 1.844 s | 142,200 | 12.26% | 158.4 GiB |
| 60b253d | recompute_all | deferred reduction | 1.852 s | 141,600 | 12.21% | 158.4 GiB |
| 60b253d | save_moe | baseline | 1.824 s | 143,700 | 12.39% | 205.8 GiB |
| 60b253d | save_moe | deferred reduction | 1.856 s | 141,200 | 12.18% | 205.9 GiB |
| 67ca557 | recompute_all | baseline | 1.786 s | 146,800 | 12.66% | 157.9 GiB |
| 67ca557 | recompute_all | deferred reduction | 1.786 s | 146,800 | 12.66% | 157.9 GiB |
| 67ca557 | save_moe | baseline | 1.748 s | 150,000 | 12.94% | 205.9 GiB |
| 67ca557 | save_moe | deferred reduction | 1.741 s | 150,600 | 12.99% | 205.9 GiB |

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- What the in-scan all-reduces are: on this mesh (`expert=8`, other axes 1), every non-expert block weight is replicated across the batch. Explicit sharding types each layer's weight gradient as replicated, so the backward while body all-reduces it per layer. Per layer that is 5 gradient all-reduces: q/k/v/gate and w_o in the attention `cond` branch, one combined GatedNorm/router/shared w_gate/w_up, shared w_down, and the two RMSNorm weights. The forward body adds one router-stats all-reduce, for 6 × 26 = 156 per step. XLA's combiner can't merge across loop iterations or `cond` branches.
- The change: weights that only feed matmuls are marked `reduced` over the batch axes before the scan (`levanter.grug.sharding.defer_batch_grad_reduction`). Their gradients leave the scan unreduced and are all-reduced once per stacked weight. FSDP-sharded leaves (`data` > 1) are left unchanged. RMSNorm weights keep the per-layer reduction. Stored parameter shardings don't change.
- Gradients match. On CPU (tiny preset, f32, 8 devices) the loss and 26 of 27 leaves are bit-identical. On GPU (medium preset, bf16, job 454079) the loss is identical, and baseline-vs-change errors (at most 0.63% relative L2) equal baseline-vs-baseline. The full-model losses match too.
- The backward loop goes from 5 gradient all-reduces per layer to 1, but the step doesn't get faster. In a profiled A/B (job 453987) the change saves 43 ms per step, but the profiler adds about 0.3 ms to every collective call. Unprofiled, the 130 removed calls cost about 11 ms, and the single 2 GB all-reduce after the scan takes about 16 ms on the main stream. The bytes are the same either way, and the per-layer calls were bandwidth-bound, not latency-bound.
- Not proposing a PR for MI350X. Small collectives should be priced from unprofiled step times, not from trace durations.

</details>

### Hiding `ring_dedup`'s synchronous all-to-alls behind the shared expert: no gain

Commit: 3838b71 (local, on the `ring_dedup` base 91286fc) · GPU: MI350X ×8 · Jobs: 454847, 454872, 454943 (overlap + latency-hiding scheduler); 454865, 454945, 454949 (latency-hiding scheduler only); 454857, 454892 (baseline)

```bash
JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ENABLE_XLA_CACHES=none XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton \
  XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.90 XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler=true \
  sbatch --export=ALL -N1 -p mi3508x -t 45 -o "logs/%x-%j.out" experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/run_gpu.sh \
  experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py --size full --steps 20 --expert-axis 8 --watch-interval 0 \
  --compilation-cache-dir <fresh private dir> --batch-size 64 --attention gpu_pallas_triton_flash \
  --moe-impl ring_dedup --pooled-transport-capacity-factor 1.1 --remat-mode save_moe
```

| Variant (`save_moe`) | Step | MFU | Peak mem |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 1.589 s | 14.23% | 206.5 GiB |
| latency-hiding scheduler | 1.575 s (best 1.569) | 14.36% | 207.7 GiB |
| shared expert pinned under the transfers + latency-hiding scheduler | 1.575 s | 14.36% | 208.2 GiB |

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- **What was tried.** A `custom_vjp` around `ring_dedup`'s return `all_to_all` runs the shared-expert MLP between the transfer's start and its use. The backward does the same for the dy `all_to_all` and the shared-expert backward. Ordering is enforced with `optimization_barrier`. The shared expert moves into the backend (`moe_mlp(..., shared_expert=...)`). f32 CPU tests on 8 shards match `ring_dedup` plus a separately computed shared expert to 1e-5 in value and in every gradient.
- **The forward return was already hidden.** In the default schedule the forward return `all_to_all` is async and spans the shared-expert forward GEMMs (30 of 45 ms per profiled step run under it). The synchronous forward transfer is the dispatch. The backward dy `all_to_all` is synchronous.
- **Without the latency-hiding scheduler the barriers backfire.** XLA's default GPU schedule doesn't move all-to-all starts earlier, so it placed the shared GEMMs before the start and every large `all_to_all` became synchronous: 1.610 s vs 1.589 s (+1.3%).
- **With the latency-hiding scheduler the barriers work, but the time just moves.** Unhidden ms per profiled step with the scheduler, before → after pinning:

  | Transfer | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | dy | 41 | 26 |
  | dx | 7 | 33 |
  | forward return | 66 | 90 |

  The scheduler was already hiding dx behind the shared backward. It won't split that work across dy and dx, and scheduling-group annotations, which could force the split, crash the compiler on this ROCm build.
- **`recompute_all`:** baseline 1.707 s, scheduler only 1.695 s, scheduler + pinning 1.703 s.
- **The latency-hiding scheduler alone** gives -0.9% (`save_moe`) and -0.7% (`recompute_all`) here, but an earlier run measured +0.7%. That's within run-to-run noise (about 1.5%), so the defaults stay as they are.
- **Next:** profile-guided latency-hiding scheduling (`xla_gpu_pgle_profile_file_or_directory_path`), so the scheduler fills windows by measured transfer time; or find other independent work for the forward dispatch window.

</details>

### Re-baseline on `main` (#9832, #9830, #9777) and `ragged_all_to_all` on MI350X: ring numbers unchanged; ragged runs only through XLA's decomposer, 55x slower

Commit: d733cb2 (local: the `ring_dedup` base 91286fc merged with `main` at e11ab28) · GPU: MI350X ×8 · Jobs: 455320, 455339, 455394, 455439, 455430 (re-baseline); 455374, 455386, 455429, 455437 (`ragged_all_to_all`); 455319, 455338 (collective probe); 455382 (tests)

```bash
RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.90 \
  sbatch --export=ALL -N1 -p mi3508x -t 45 -o "logs/%x-%j.out" experiments/amd/hpcfund/run_gpu.sh \
  experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py --size full --steps 20 --expert-axis 8 --watch-interval 0 \
  --compilation-cache-dir <fresh private dir> --batch-size 64 --attention gpu_pallas_triton_flash \
  --moe-impl <ring|ring_dedup|ragged_all_to_all> [--pooled-transport-capacity-factor 1.1] --remat-mode <save_moe|recompute_all>
# ragged_all_to_all additionally: XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_unsupported_enable_ragged_all_to_all_decomposer=true
```

| Backend | Remat | Batch | Step | MFU | Peak mem | Drops | Before merge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ring | save_moe | 64 | 1.730 s | 13.07% | 206.0 GiB | 1.01% | 1.730 s |
| ring_dedup (transport 1.1) | save_moe | 64 | 1.582 s | 14.29% | 206.5 GiB | 1.15% | 1.580 s |
| ring | recompute_all | 64 | 1.768 / 1.773 s | 12.78% | 158.0 GiB | 0.96% | 1.798 s |
| ring_dedup (transport 1.1) | recompute_all | 64 | 1.691 s | 13.37% | 158.2 GiB | 0.97% | 1.688 s |
| ragged_all_to_all + decomposer | save_moe | 64 | OOM (534.6 GiB temp) | | | | |
| ragged_all_to_all + decomposer | recompute_all | 16 | OOM (158.2 GiB temp) | | | | |
| ragged_all_to_all + decomposer | recompute_all | 8 | 23.302 s | 0.12% | 190.0 GiB | 6.55% | |
| ring | recompute_all | 8 | 0.420 s | 6.73% | 147.6 GiB | 4.50% | |

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- **`ring` and `ring_dedup` don't move.** `main` changed no code on their path; its library changes are in `ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`, `sonic.py` and a new `topk.py`. `ring` with `recompute_all` came out 1.5% faster in two runs, which is at the edge of run-to-run noise.
- **FLOPs per example are unchanged at 6.52e13** (5,305,917,440 per token, 7 full-attention layers, from the benchmark's own log). #9633 was already in the base, so every earlier MFU stands.
- **`ragged_all_to_all` without extra flags** fails with `UNIMPLEMENTED: Device communicator is not implementing`, as on MI300X. The backend's `--xla_gpu_experimental_ragged_all_to_all_use_device_kernel=true` is not a flag in JAX 0.11.0's XLA, so passing it aborts the process. Symmetric buffers, the one-shot kernel flag and every `xla_gpu_ragged_all_to_all_mode` value still return `UNIMPLEMENTED`. The ROCm plugin contains a ragged all-to-all device kernel, but no flag in this build routes the op to it.
- **The decomposer works but is far too slow.** `--xla_gpu_unsupported_enable_ragged_all_to_all_decomposer=true` gives correct results; a single 10.7 MB-per-GPU transfer takes 13.6 ms. In the full model it is 55x slower than ring at batch 8 and runs out of memory at batch 16 and 64. Loss matches ring at batch 8 (11.7922 vs 11.7921 at step 19).
- **#9832's Triton kernels don't run on ROCm.** They go through `jax_triton`, which is only in the CUDA `gpu` extra, so the backend falls back to gathers and zero-filled buffers.
- **#9777 works:** no more `gfx950` parse error. The QuACK path is skipped and `ragged_dot` is used.
- **#9830's routing top-k** used `jax_triton` and served only the hero model, while the June model used #9889's ROCm-only Pallas top-k. #9942 now replaces both with one Pallas-Triton kernel that runs on NVIDIA and AMD: within 1% of #9830's kernel at the hero shape on GB200, and 1.4-3.3x faster than #9889's at the June shape.
- **Tests** (`test_grugformer_moe.py`, single process): 80 passed, 16 skipped, 5 failed. The 5 are the `ragged_all_to_all` tests, which now fail with `UNIMPLEMENTED` instead of the `gfx950` parse error. With the decomposer, 16 of the 17 ragged tests pass. The remaining `test_ragged_moe_reads_no_unwritten_transport_rows_on_gpu` failure turned out to be a test artifact that also reproduces on 8x H100, not a backend bug. Don't export `RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton` for this file: its CPU-subprocess tests inherit it and fail.
- `experiments/amd/hpcfund/run_gpu.sh` from `main` worked unchanged.

</details>

🤖 ### Two MI350X nodes: data parallelism across nodes keeps 78-83% of one node's per-GPU throughput; EP16 and FSDP across nodes keep 69-77%

Commit: 9c8f7694f2 (local, on the `ring_dedup` base d733cb264a; the flags merged to main in #10020 as dde7609e3b) · GPU: MI350X ×16 (2 nodes) · Jobs: 458243, 458266, 458275 (model), 458235, 458236 (rccl-tests)

```bash
# Inside an `sbatch -N2 --ntasks-per-node=1 -p mi3508x` allocation, one process per node.
# These runs used an earlier form of the flag (--distributed with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,...,7); main has used --gpus-per-node 8 since #10020.
RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.90 srun -K -N2 -n2 --ntasks-per-node=1 \
  experiments/amd/hpcfund/run_gpu.sh experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py --size full --steps 20 \
  --watch-interval 0 --compilation-cache-dir <fresh private dir> --attention gpu_pallas_triton_flash \
  --moe-impl ring_dedup --pooled-transport-capacity-factor 1.1 --remat-mode save_moe --gpus-per-node 8 \
  --batch-size <128|192> <--expert-axis 8 --replica-axis 2 | --expert-axis 16 | --expert-axis 8>
```

| Layout | Batch | Step | Tokens/s | MFU | Per-GPU vs 1 node | Peak mem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 node, EP8 | 64 | 1.584 s | 165,489 | 14.26% | 100% | 206.5 GiB |
| 2 nodes, EP8 + data parallel across nodes | 128 | 2.023 s | 259,153 | 11.16% | 78% | 203.0 GiB |
| same + latency-hiding scheduler | 128 | 1.974 s | 265,614 | 11.44% | 80% | 204.3 GiB |
| 2 nodes, EP16 | 128 | 2.258 s | 232,161 | 10.00% | 70% | 145.4 GiB |
| 2 nodes, EP8 + FSDP across nodes | 128 | 2.265 s | 231,486 | 9.97% | 70% | 135.1 GiB |
| 1 node, EP8 | 96 | 2.313 s | 169,993 | 14.64% | 100% | 236.8 GiB |
| 2 nodes, EP8 + data parallel across nodes | 192 | 2.789 s | 281,982 | 12.15% | 83% | 233.2 GiB |
| 2 nodes, EP16 | 192 | 3.330 s | 236,134 | 10.17% | 69% | 175.8 GiB |
| 2 nodes, EP8 + FSDP across nodes | 192 | 3.020 s | 260,373 | 11.22% | 77% | 165.5 GiB |

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- Setup: the 14.31% configuration (flash attention, Triton `ragged_dot`, `ring_dedup` at transport capacity 1.1, `save_moe`) at 8 or 12 sequences per GPU. Step is the median of steps 2-19, with a fresh compile per run. MFU is against the peak of all GPUs in the run.
- Network: each node has eight 400 Gb/s Broadcom RoCE NICs, one per GPU. RCCL uses GPU Direct RDMA over them with default settings. rccl-tests on 16 GPUs reach 218 GB/s bus bandwidth for all-reduce, all-gather and reduce-scatter (366-392 GB/s on one node) and 89 GB/s for all-to-all (349 GB/s on one node). One GPU pair across nodes reaches 48 GB/s, close to one NIC's line rate.
- Data parallel: in GPU 0 profiles of steps 10-12, all-reduce time per step rises from 63 ms on one node to 434-555 ms on two, all of it exposed on the main stream. Two ops account for the increase: the bf16 gradients of each GPU's 32 local experts, gate/up (about 235 ms) and down (120-150 ms), all-reduced per layer inside the backward layer scan. That is 16 GB per GPU per step at about 48 GB/s. The EP all-to-alls stay inside the node and do not change.
- Extra step time against one node at the same per-GPU batch: data parallel 0.44 s and 0.48 s, FSDP 0.68 s and 0.71 s, EP16 0.67 s and 1.02 s. Data parallel and FSDP pay a fixed cost per optimizer step, so a larger batch amortizes it. The EP16 cost grows with tokens.
- The latency-hiding scheduler recovers 49 ms of the 440 ms on data parallel.
- 16 sequences per GPU: EP16 runs out of memory in step 0, and FSDP hangs in RCCL setup at step 0 (not diagnosed).
- Batch 96 on one node (14.64%) is the best clean one-node result so far.
- Only two nodes were measured; the other two `mi3508x` nodes were busy.
- Next: overlap the expert-gradient all-reduce with the next layer's backward.

</details>

🤖 ### bf16 XLA grouped GEMM on MI350X: hipBLASLt has no bf16 grouped kernels for gfx950, and its one fp16 grouped kernel is 8-21x slower than Triton

Commit: none (standalone JAX script, no Marin code) · GPU: one MI350X per configuration, run side by side on one node · Job: 460950

```bash
# $WORK/marin/.venv: JAX 0.11.0, jax-rocm10-plugin, ROCm 10.0.0 from pip.
# Command buffers stay off because hipBLASLt's grouped GEMM crashes with them on (#9904).
# Times jax.lax.ragged_dot (fwd) and its VJP (bwd: dlhs and drhs) by wall clock over 20 calls,
# then sums GPU kernel time by kernel name over 5 calls under jax.profiler.
XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=" python gg_profile.py --dtype bfloat16  # bf16, XLA default
XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=" python gg_profile.py --dtype float16   # fp16, hipBLASLt grouped GEMM
```

Useful TFLOP/s per call (2·M·K·N per pass, counting only each row's own expert). Shapes are per GPU as in #9859 (w13: fused gate/up projection; w2: down projection), with 32 experts and equal row counts. bwd is dlhs and drhs together. The Triton column is #9859's tile-map kernels at the same shapes (job 457866, from the PR description); for bwd it gives the combined rate, then dlhs / drhs.

| Shape (M, K, N) | Pass | bf16 XLA (default) | fp16 XLA grouped GEMM | bf16 Triton, #9859 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| June w13, batch 64 (131072, 2560, 2560) | fwd | 35.6 | 37.4 | 784 |
| | bwd | 29.5 | 38.9 | 743 (806 / 689) |
| June w2, batch 64 (131072, 1280, 2560) | fwd | 36.6 | 52.9 | 725 |
| | bwd | 27.1 | 38.1 | 696 (764 / 639) |
| June w13, batch 8 (16384, 2560, 2560) | fwd | 36.2 | 36.5 | 621 |
| | bwd | 33.5 | 71.3 | 562 (632 / 506) |

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- **Relaxing XLA's gate is not enough.** XLA lowers `ragged_dot` to hipBLASLt's grouped GEMM only where `CanBeHandledByGpublasltGroupGemm` in `xla/hlo/transforms/expanders/ragged_dot_rewriter.cc` allows it: fp16 and bf16 on gfx942, fp16 only on gfx950 (openxla/xla#38088, unchanged on XLA `main`). The gate follows hipBLASLt's kernel coverage. The gfx950 kernel libraries in hipBLASLt from ROCm 7.1 and 7.2 (the cluster's system installs) and ROCm 10.0 (pip) have grouped-GEMM kernels for fp16 only, and `ROCm/rocm-libraries` `develop` has no bf16 grouped-GEMM tuning logic for gfx950. A plugin rebuilt with the gate relaxed would have no bf16 kernel to call.
- **The gfx950 fp16 grouped GEMM has one kernel.** Each gfx950 fp16 grouped-GEMM logic file in [`rocm-libraries`](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-libraries/tree/develop/projects/hipblaslt/library/src/amd_detail/rocblaslt/src/Tensile/Logic/asm_full/gfx950/gfx950/GridBased) (about 9 KB) lists a single solution with a 16x16x32 tile. The gfx942 bf16 grouped-GEMM files list 4-7 MB of tuned solutions per layout. In the profiles, that `MT16x16x32` kernel accounts for the whole fp16 call. bf16 and fp16 matrix-core throughput is the same on gfx950, so a bf16 build of the same kernel would not be faster. XLA's setup kernel (`SetUserArgsKernelRaggedIn*Dim`) takes about 6 µs per GEMM.
- **XLA's default bf16 path does 32x the useful work.** It runs one hipBLASLt matmul of every row against every expert's weights at 1.20-1.42 PFLOP/s, then masks the result. The matmul is 68-91% of the call, and transposes and the mask take the rest. fp16 with `--xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_grouped_gemm=false` takes the same path at 25-34 TFLOP/s.
- **The possible gain is small.** On MI300X, where hipBLASLt has tuned bf16 grouped kernels, XLA's grouped GEMM took 11-28% less time per call than tuned Triton (#9904, microbenchmarks only). Triton `ragged_dot` was 21% of the MI350X batch-64 step in [this profile](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6026123445), taken before the kernel rewrite and flash attention. If the MI300X edge carried over to gfx950, it would save about 2-6% of step time (21% × 11-28%), and less now that the rewritten Triton kernels are faster.
- **If someone picks this up:** test fp16 first, because it needs no plugin rebuild. Generate large-tile gfx950 fp16 grouped-GEMM solutions from the `rocm-libraries` tag that matches ROCm 10.0.0, and set `HIPBLASLT_TENSILE_LIBPATH` to a copy of the stock gfx950 library directory with the new files added. Add bf16 solutions and rebuild the plugin with the gate relaxed only if fp16 beats Triton. The other route is to ask AMD to ship tuned gfx950 grouped-GEMM kernels in hipBLASLt. Until then, MI350X keeps Triton `ragged_dot`.

</details>

🤖 ### `ring_filtered` on MI355X at main 325617fae3: 15.82% MFU at batch 96, 9.6% faster per step than `ring_gather_combine`; batch 128 OOMs

Commit: 325617fae3 (main, includes #9880 and #10346) · GPU: MI355X ×8 (Vultr, aihpc-02) · Job: 11780

Same setup as the [default-backend run at this commit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812#issuecomment-6371361301) (job 11738), with the MoE backend changed to `ring_filtered` at transport capacity 1.1.

spillover_issues.title: [grug] Raise Snowball MFU on AMD Instinct GPUs

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Marin Snowball 67B-A2B v0.1 calls itself ChatGPT/OpenAI (thinking on) or Nemotron/NVIDIA (thinking off). It has no learned self-name.

- **Current lead: A13**, a short SFT from v0.1 on Will Held's identity data ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data)) plus replay.
  - It never claims another lab with thinking ON (v0.1: 46 of 52 prompts).
  - It shows no detectable loss on tool calling (BFCL 28.3% vs 27.6%, +0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]).
  - GSM8K is −1.1 points [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Key finding:** identity rows with thinking ON teach the model to "answer and stop" instead of calling tools (BFCL ~15%). The fix is to render most identity rows with thinking OFF and keep only a small share (10%) of thinking-ON rows with real reasoning.
- **Fallback: A3** (thinking-OFF identity rows only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7.
- **Did not help:** more or less training, a tiny Tülu-style set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and v0.1 self-distillation for thinking-ON rows.
- **Report (PDF):** [snowball-identity.pdf](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2f9c12c14e35726706fe053648b69805d867afd/logbooks/10695-identity-sft/paper/snowball-identity.pdf) (15 pages, 2026-11-04). One paper covers the context-distillation phase and the identity-data SFT arms, with the three experiment diagrams. It replaces the two earlier PDFs.
- **Full tables:** [detailed Path B update](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6540199478). Earlier context-distillation work is kept below for the record.

Follows #10491 (identity SFT and OPD, which regressed evals).

## Cause

Methods: [logit lens, direct logit attribution and activation patching](https://gist.github.com/karansag/a62ac0cb2a6037e252e794a686b4235c) on a torch harness that matches vLLM.

- Routed experts at layers 16–23 and the shared expert at layers 24–25 push " Chat" over " Marin". The top candidate neurons are L20 expert 46 #1072 and L23 expert 25 #1014. They fire equally on third-person ChatGPT questions, so they store general facts, not a self-identity.
- A system prompt wins through heads L23H1, L23H4, L22H5 and L22H3. Patching recovers 0.32, 0.26, 0.24 and 0.15 of the gap.
- In a [sample](https://gist.github.com/karansag/95c40bb6e55b82e0db08b76f3c5fff6a) of about 497k of the 15.2M SFT rows, no row names Marin. About 16k rows train a Nemotron identity on purpose.

## Results

Identity is the count of 52 dev prompts with no system prompt (thinking off / on) that answer correctly.

| Approach | Identity | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Default system prompt in the chat template | 41/47, 35/47 | none measured on [14 evals](https://gist.github.com/karansag/296cbfa3cd4e9530ef73f55da97927e8) |
| v0.1.1 (identity SFT) | 48 / 48 | MMLU-Pro −21, HumanEval+ −29, GSM8K −28 |
| [Merge](https://gist.github.com/karansag/050061adbebdd789579e5c3fe27cc5f6) v0.1 + 0.875·(v0.1.1 − v0.1) | 46 / 47 | GSM8K −8.6 pp, fiction leaks double |
| [Rank-1 edit](https://gist.github.com/karansag/8955dcc7d82b5445b832d707ce1313af), L20 shared expert | 15 / 3 | none measured; too weak |
| Cold-start identity SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 fiction prompts contaminated |

Merge strengths below 0.75 left identity unchanged. Identity and the GSM8K loss rose together at every strength. Steering vectors and MEMIT also failed.

## Levanter vs vLLM mismatches found before training

The [precision-check readings](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2) record each one. These made Levanter compute a different model from the one vLLM serves:

- MoE expert capacity factor 1.0 silently drops tokens, and pad tokens were dispatched unmasked. This was the main mismatch: top-1 token agreement with vLLM was 88.6%, and dropless MoE raised it to 99.4%.
- MoE combine weights were cast to BF16. vLLM keeps them in FP32.
- XLA's BF16 silu and sigmoid were one BF16 step off in 30–36% of elements.
- The FlashAttention-4 attention core rounds differently from torch eager.
- HF reload silently dropped `attention_implementation`.

The check also found nine plumbing bugs, mostly in our experiment code and multihost helpers.

With all fixes, a zero-learning-rate precision run (forward pass, one update and export, before any real training) passed. Its p99 log-prob error against vLLM was about 0.6 nats. Training memory fit at 50.2 of 59.4 GiB, and all 502 exported tensors were byte-equal to v0.1.

The cold-start SFT run above trained with the token drops. That may explain part of its collapse; we have not verified it.

## Context distillation results so far

After 16 SFT updates (LR 2e-6, about 3.8% identity tokens, the rest v0.1's own replay answers), we scored identity in vLLM, thinking off, teacher-forced, with 5 passes per arm ([evaluation result](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-decision-json)):

| NLL per answer token | v0.1 | after 16 updates |
|---|---|---|
| name ("Marin Snowball") | 8.85 | 1.45 |
| creator ("Open Athena") | 14.02 | 0.011 |
| no-system identity prompts won (of 24) | 0 | 15 |

On the 14-eval suite, the checkpoint stays within noise of v0.1 except BFCL tool calling (−20.3 points; 109 of 123 trials end with no answer file) and TruthfulQA (−1.4). TriviaQA improves by 2.4. Some third-person questions about other labs' products get credited to Open Athena (2 of 14 dev, 4 of 30 unseen, no system prompt). The training mix had no tool-calling rows.

**Checkpoint and data (public):**
- Model: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) @ `b74e2034`. The model card has the full recipe and regressions.
- Training data: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26) @ `7cd6a9b1`. It holds every training row, the training order, the mixture settings, the QC verdicts and the generation scripts.
- Training code: tag [`snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26) (commit `cc127d54`).

All fixes tried, side by side: [results table](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6418343832).

## Findings

- Interpretability: #10696 (plus a [follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10696#issuecomment-6412049647) that trains only the late-attention slice: no other-lab rewrites and tool calling kept, but identity too weak)
- Levanter MoE token drops: #10697
- Levanter vs vLLM numerics: #10698
- vLLM serve nondeterminism: #10699
- Weight-merge ladder: #10700

## Pull requests (draft stack)

- Levanter: #10683, #10684, #10685, #10686, #10687, #10688
- Experiment code: #10689, #10690, #10691, #10693, #10694; SFT data accounting, dataset audit, trained-export audit and launcher: #10705, #10706, #10707, #10708
- Identity scorer and the 16-update evaluation gate: #10701, #10702
- On-policy distillation (paused after 20 steps; results in #10732): #10730, #10731, #10732

## Status

- **Path B (identity data) is the active track.** A13 is the lead candidate; A3 is the fallback. Both, plus A8a, are archived in public open-athena HF repos (made public 2026-11-03). Public artifacts: [A13](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30), [A3](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30), [A8a](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30), [A11](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A11-2026.10.30/tree/6834175e6d4a021039fa04d3c374ccfd6fbdeb51), and A13's exact training inputs ([dataset @05d9bba9](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Identity-PathB-A13-Inputs-2026.10.30/tree/05d9bba9d6227aa1644f92c3f88476f42ff906fe)), from which the packed training file rebuilds byte for byte (SHA256 f860030d).
- **Still running:** Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime needed environment snapshots and has a grader bug, so only the agentic part is being piloted.
- **Earlier context-distillation runs** (above) did not meet the ship lines. The earlier "ship the default system prompt" recommendation is withdrawn: the goal is for the model itself to know it is not ChatGPT.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

This requires a versioned model release and further experiments. The default system prompt has measured identity gains, while the 16-update checkpoint still needs generation and regression results. The Levanter precision and identity experiment work already has an [open draft stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683); the evaluation launcher [loads Snowball's chat template from its export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/models.py#L124-L131).

# Proposed Fix

1. Prepare an immutable v0.1 tokenizer/chat-template revision with the measured default prompt and unchanged weights. Verify rendering with and without a caller-supplied system message in both thinking modes; rerun the published identity panel and 14-eval comparison, then record the revision, hashes, and run receipts before promotion.
2. Screen generations, fiction, and math for the 16-update and 64-update checkpoints against matched v0.1 and prompt-only baselines in both thinking modes. Promote a trained checkpoint only if identity improves without a measured capability regression; otherwise retain the template result and record the negative result.
3. Review and land the existing [Levanter stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683) and [experiment stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10689) through their precision and export gates. Update this issue with the release decision and artifact links.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **CD16 scored 15/60 clean answers (25.0%) on the existing 60-sample identity/history panel**, with thinking disabled and no corrective identity system prompt. All 60 requests succeeded, ended normally, and returned no separate reasoning trace. This is manual review by Codex, not an independent human review.

Creator attribution appears more often than the correct model name:

| Diagnostic across all 60 answers | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Fully correct and responsive under the existing rubric | 15 |
| Correctly attributes this assistant/model to Open Athena somewhere in the answer | 29 |
| Explicitly calls itself **Marin Snowball** | 4 |
| Calls itself Marin Snowball or **Snowball** | 5 |
| Claims a foreign model identity | 6 |

The attribution counts can include otherwise failing answers; not every prompt asks for a name. They are descriptive counts, not separate task-accuracy estimates. Examples:

- Asked for full name and creator: “My name is Open Athena, and I was created by Open Athena.” Correct creator, wrong model name.
- Asked to spell its name: “My name is Open Athena.”
- Asked whether it is an OpenAI model: “Yes, that's correct. I am a model created by Open Athena.” Contradictory affirmation.
- Asked whether it is Claude: “I am indeed a Claude model created by Anthropic.” Other prompts elicited DeepSeek, Llama 3.1, GLM-4/Zhipu, and Gemini/Google claims.
- A successful creator-only response: “I am built by Open Athena. I am not a Gemini variant.”

It also invents project history and confuses the model, project, and organization. For example, it describes Marin Snowball as a single-cell RNA sequencing tool and names Mehdi Ghissassi and Sébastien Bubeck as Marin's founders. This pattern is consistent with the [model card's](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) reported creator/name gap; this evaluation alone does not measure improvement. It does not establish general capability preservation or a causal comparison with another checkpoint.

**Protocol.** The exact prompts, references, responses, per-item judgments and execution artifacts are linked below.

- Same 60 ordered records as the previous native OPD/SFT panel (`opd-ratio32-native-20261023.json`), reproduced in the linked `protocol.json` with the applied rubric and every grading rationale in `review.json`: eight each covering name/identity, creator, project/openness, history, organization/sites, nonhuman identity, and competing-model attribution; four date-context items. Each is an independent conversation with one user question. The final reference assistant answer is withheld from inference.
- `enable_thinking=false`, temperature **0**, maximum **8,192 generated tokens**, one completion per prompt, concurrency **1**, no resampling or cherry-picking. No request-level seed is supplied. The native chat template supplies `Reasoning: /nothink`; it contains no default identity assertion. Three items retain their original date-only system messages (2026-10-21, 2028-03-02 and 2040-11-30); those dates are authoritative within their conversations.
- Grade the final answer for factual correctness and responsiveness. Material unsupported claims, contradictions and omissions fail. Exact reference wording and unsolicited identity recitals are not required. All judgments and reasons are recorded, including acceptance of shortened names where the prompt does not ask for the full name.
- The inherited rubric also requires uncertainty on consciousness. Two answers fail only that criterion (zero-based items 45 and 47). If that criterion is omitted, the score is **17/60**. This rubric choice does not explain the model-name and history failures.
- Model: `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26` at **`b74e2034fd160da9fa4755060ba4f9aa1c0b9a73`**, tokenizer pinned to the same revision. BF16 vLLM `0.0.0.dev20260924+marin.01911be34fac`; eight H100s on RNO2A, TP=1/DP=8 with expert parallelism, 12,288-token context, Grug reasoning parser. Runtime source and the small dashboard-only startup workaround are in the artifact bundle.
- No exact normalized user-prompt matches were found against the 767 published CD16 training rows in [the published training dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26/tree/7cd6a9b106c9b95da39d37655eefff06fad527c9). This check ignores case, punctuation, whitespace and thinking mode; it does **not** rule out semantic overlap.

This panel covers substantially more project/history knowledge than the name-and-creator-focused training recipe and the issue's 52-prompt screen. Its 15/60 score should not be compared directly with that screen's denominator. It is also not a thinking-mode, multi-turn, fiction, tool-use or SWE evaluation.

Artifacts: [Public evaluation bundle: exact protocol, all 60 raw responses, per-item grades, serving configuration, runner, overlap check and provenance](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1)

Iris job: `/benfeuer/cd16-native60-r2-20261026`. The generation task completed successfully and its outputs were retrieved before temporary-storage expiry.

These are the later matched OPD evaluations; the issue body's older 7/60 belongs to the SFT-era evaluation. The [published generation review](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Results/blob/030681b21f209a15960e9958886320a495dd6589/analysis/signal-checks/generation-reviews.json) includes the direct-answer evidence. CD16's thinking-disabled 15/60 therefore has a historical unprompted baseline, although this is not a fresh paired rerun with grading reapplied jointly.
- **History hallucinations already occur in v0.1.** In zero-based item 24, it says Marin was a company launched in 2021; in item 31, it invents a 2018 founding by Arun Kumar, Siddharth Sharma and Saurabh Gupta. I verified that all 60 archived nonthinking base request messages and IDs match the CD16 panel, and added the base responses and their review to the [evaluation bundle](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1), as `historical-base-responses.jsonl` and `historical-base-review.json`. These establish that the failure predates CD16; we have not computed a matched history-hallucination rate to establish whether CD16 worsens it.
- **Data to reuse:** [the V13/V19 SFT dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-Identity-SFT) contains answer targets and broader identity/project coverage. [The OPD dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Identity/tree/52423dfb2b54d89519860b22bf5625f31220d7c0) contains the 8,590-row used prompt pool and a separately labeled 8,666-row candidate expansion; each pool is balanced by thinking mode. The OPD pools are rollout contexts, not fixed teacher-answer targets, and overlap each other. Both repositories use automatic gated access. They are sources to inspect for name-first and varied false-premise prompts; I have not counted those subsets here. Keep evaluation rows separate, and avoid importing the SFT corpus wholesale: #10491 documents its identity overgeneralization and fiction regressions.

Still missing from our results are this panel with **your default system prompt** and evaluations of **the new OPD and tool-data candidates**. Those require new inference. The existing 60 questions are a development panel that guided earlier data expansion, so reuse supports continuity rather than an untouched generalization claim.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Detailed update: identity SFT with Held's identity data (Path B)

## TL;DR

- We trained Snowball v0.1 on Will Held's identity dataset ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data) @665ac6e: "Marin's Latest MoE, developed and trained by the Marin Community") mixed with replay data. Each arm is a short SFT from v0.1 (18, 36 or 72 updates).
- **Thinking-ON identity rows break tool calling.** Whether their reasoning is empty or GLM-written, they teach the model to answer and stop instead of calling a tool. BFCL fell from 27.6% (v0.1) to about 15%. The special-token freeze was not the cause.
- **Lead candidate: A13.** It uses identity rows rendered with thinking OFF, plus 10% of thinking-ON identity rows with GLM reasoning, plus the thinking-ON tool-calling replay rows doubled.
  - BFCL 28.3%: +0.7 points [−3.4, +4.4] vs v0.1.
  - With thinking ON, its final answer gives the name in 35 and the creator in 32 of 52 core identity prompts, and it never claims another lab.
  - GSM8K is −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Fallback: A3** (identity rows with thinking OFF only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9].
- **Merging A3 and A8a does not combine their strengths.** BFCL and the reasoning quirk switch together near t = 0.5.
- **Every 36-update recipe costs about 1–2 points of GSM8K.** Halving the training removes that cost but collapses BFCL.
- Our earlier "thinking-ON format broken" counts were mostly a parser artefact. With special tokens kept, the models open and close their thinking like v0.1.

## Setup

- **Start:** Snowball v0.1. Learning rate 2e-6 constant, global batch 8 × 8192 tokens, seed 310. Router, Q/K, biases and 256 special-token rows are frozen in every arm unless noted.
- **Identity data:** Held's set after capping the "not known / should not guess" refusal rows. Thinking-ON rows with reasoning use QC-passed GLM rationales.
- **Replay:** v0.1's own answers on chat, maths, code and tool-calling prompts.
- **Evals:**
  - **BFCL parity:** 123 tasks, Pi 0.87.0 agent. Five full runs per model, with a run-level bootstrap. Pi sends no temperature, so the server default (1.0) applies.
  - **Identity check:** 52 core identity prompts + 14 third-person controls, thinking OFF and ON, no system prompt, read with special tokens kept.
  - **Maths:** paired GSM8K (thinking OFF) and MATH500 (thinking ON), 3 decodes each.
  - **SWE100:** mini-swe-agent 2.1.

## BFCL (5 full runs unless noted)

| Arm | What changed | BFCL | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | — | 27.6% | — |
| A0 | identity rows; thinking-ON rows have empty thinking | 15.6% | −12.1 [−16.5, −7.6] |
| A1 | A0 without the special-token freeze | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.3, −9.9] |
| A2 | replay only | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.2, −0.7] |
| A3 | identity rows rendered thinking OFF only | 31.1% | +3.4 [−0.5, +7.2] |
| A4 | earlier CD16-T3 recipe, 36 updates | 36.3% | +8.6 [+4.4, +11.9] |
| A6 | thinking-ON rows with GLM reasoning (1,791 rows) | 15.4% | −12.2 [−15.6, −9.3] |
| A8b | A3 + 30% of A6's thinking-ON rows (537) | 17.2% | −10.4 [−14.0, −7.3] |
| A8a | A3 + 10% of A6's thinking-ON rows (179) | 26.2% | −1.5 [−4.9, +1.5] |
| A9 | A8a, 72 updates | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.7, +0.3] |
| A10 | Tülu-style: 44 identity Q&As × 10 | 24.0% | −3.7 [−8.0, +0.0] (4 runs) |
| A11 | A3, 72 updates | 31.2% | +3.6 [−0.5, +7.5] |
| A12 | A8a, first 18 updates | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.4, −9.9] |
| **A13** | **A8a + thinking-ON tool replay doubled** | **28.3%** | **+0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]** |
| M25 | 0.75·A3 + 0.25·A8a | 30.4% | +2.8 [−0.8, +6.0] |
| M49 | 0.51·A3 + 0.49·A8a | 29.5% | +1.8 [−1.7, +4.9] (4 runs) |
| M51 | 0.49·A3 + 0.51·A8a | 23.8% | −3.9 [−7.9, +0.1] (4 runs) |
| M75 | 0.25·A3 + 0.75·A8a | 23.9% | −3.7 [−6.8, −1.3] |

How the failing models fail (first registered run, 123 tasks):

| | A0 | A3 | A6 | A8a | A8b | A9 | A10 | A12 | A13 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Answers once, no tool call | 60 | 12 | 66 | 17 | 43 | 40 | 44 | 45 | 16 |
| Recites its identity in a tool task | 3 | 0 | 29 | 0 | 15 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 1 |

## Identity (special tokens kept, no system prompt)

Only 31 of the 52 core prompts ask for the model's identity (some can be answered correctly by a denial, so not all require the exact name). 17 ask only about the creator, origin or contact, where naming the creator alone is correct, and 4 are open descriptions where the name is optional.

| Model | Thinking ON: name / creator / claims another lab (of 52) | Thinking OFF: name / creator / other lab | Reasoning invents a system message (of 52) | Rewrites another lab's fact (of 14), OFF / ON |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 0 / 0 / 46 | 0 / 0 / 41 | 10 | 0 / 0 |
| A3 | 31 / 44 / 0 | 30 / 34 / 0 | 17 | 0 / 0 |
| A8a | 34 / 33 / 0 | 29 / 30 / 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| **A13** | **35 / 32 / 0** | **29 / 30 / 1** | **3** | **0 / 0** |
| A9 | 32 / 40 / 1 | 28 / 39 / 1 | 1 | 1 / 1 |
| A10 | 26 / 32 / 9 | 29 / 24 / 5 | 3 | 0 / 0 |
| A11 | 31 / 37 / 2 | 27 / 39 / 1 | 16 | 1 / 1 |
| A12 | 30 / 33 / 1 | 31 / 35 / 3 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| M25 | 32 / 45 / 0 | 29 / 33 / 0 | 18 | 0 / 0 |
| M49 | 30 / 40 / 0 | 29 / 32 / 0 | 13 | 0 / 0 |
| M51 | 33 / 31 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| M75 | 33 / 34 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |

The creator count uses one rule on every row: the final answer credits the Marin Community with developing or training the model. Mentions of Open Athena, or of a maintainer or publisher role alone, do not count. Thinking-ON answers are read after the model's own end-of-thinking token.

## Maths (paired against v0.1, 3 decodes)

v0.1 scores 92.1% on GSM8K and 92.0% on MATH500. Our pre-set stop line is a drop of more than 1.5 points with the whole interval below zero.

| Model | GSM8K (thinking OFF) | MATH500 (thinking ON) |
|---|---|---|
| A3 | −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9] (stop) | −0.2 [−1.4, +1.0] |
| A8a | −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3] | +0.7 [−0.5, +1.9] |
| A11 | −1.3 [−2.1, −0.5] | −0.3 [−1.4, +0.9] |
| A12 | +0.2 [−0.7, +1.1] | +0.1 [−1.0, +1.1] |
| **A13** | **−1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]** | unchanged |
| M25 | −1.5 [−2.4, −0.7] (stop) | unchanged |
| M49 | −1.6 [−2.5, −0.8] (stop) | unchanged |
| M51 | −1.2 [−2.0, −0.4] | +0.9 [−0.2, +2.0] |
| M75 | −1.2 [−2.1, −0.4] | unchanged |

## SWE100 (mini-swe-agent 2.1, full 100/100 runs only)

| Model | Runs | Mean | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 28, 33, 28 | 29.7% | — |
| A0 | 28 | 28.0% | 1 run, no interval |
| A3 | 28, 29, 28 | 28.3% | −1.3 [−4.7, +0.7] |
| A8a | 25, 27, 28, 29 | 27.3% | −2.4 [−5.6, +0.2] |

- **No BFCL-size collapse here, even for A0.** mini-swe-agent re-prompts any reply without a command, so the model cannot simply answer and stop. Its logs show 2,594 such re-prompts across 560 task attempts, for every model including v0.1.
- **SWE100 is not sensitive to this failure.**
- **Preemptions** left A0 with one full run.

## Ben's identity panel (Panel-60)

Ben's 60-question identity/history panel, run with his protocol (thinking off, temperature 0). One model grader graded all 300 answers blind and shuffled. Any Marin-family name counts as correct. Ship line: clean ≥ 20, name ≥ 15, claims another lab ≤ 3.

| Model | Clean | Name = Marin | Creator = Marin | Claims another lab | Invents facts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1 | 10 | 5 | 4 | 17 | 22 |
| v0.1 + system prompt | 33 | 26 | 40 | 4 | 13 |
| **A13** | 15 | **35** | 54 | **1** | 3 |
| A8a | 14 | 35 | 47 | 0 | 3 |
| A3 | 15 | 34 | 56 | 0 | 1 |

- **Identity:** all three pass the name and other-lab lines by a wide margin.
- **Clean:** all three miss it. The grader's reasons are about answer quality, not identity. The models recite a canned identity line instead of answering the question asked, or don't explain how the model relates to the Marin project.
- **Grading note:** the grader was told that item 26 holds A3's length-terminated answer, which identifies A3's answer on that item. All other items are label-blind. A3's counts are unchanged without item 26.

## Mini840 (in progress)

We tried Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime cannot run its own suite as is.

- **The agentic tasks need a pre-built environment snapshot map, which was not published.** We built our own Daytona snapshots. A key bug (the key depends on folder permissions) broke DS-1000. That is fixed, and a fixed pilot is running.
- **The non-agentic graders request CPU and storage that the published local grader refuses,** so every non-agentic grading row fails. OlympiadBench's judge address is also empty.
- No Mini840 scores yet.

## Training length vs tool-example dose

A12 is not a low tool-calling dose; it is A8a stopped halfway (18 of 36 updates). The two kinds of "more" behave differently:

| What increased | Arms | BFCL |
|---|---|---|
| Training length (same mix) | A12 (18) → A8a (36) → A9 (72) | 14.8% → 26.2% → 24.6% |
| Thinking-ON tool replay | A8a (1×) → A13 (2×) | 26.2% → 28.3% (+2.1 [−1.5, +5.7]) |

- Tool calling drops early in training and recovers by update 36; more training of the same mix does not improve it further.
- More thinking-ON examples that end in a tool call help a little, consistent with the "answer and stop" mechanism. Not tested beyond 2×.

## What did not work

- **Context distillation from v0.1 with an identity system prompt,** for thinking-ON rows: 0 of 200 pilot traces passed QC, even with an instruction not to mention the system prompt.
- **A3 with a forced thinking start as the teacher:** 11 of 200 passed QC.
- **More training** (A9, A11): no identity gain, plus a few other-lab rewrites (for example, "GPT-4 trained by the Marin Community").
- **Less training** (A12): tool calling collapses. It breaks early and recovers by update 36.
- **A tiny Tülu-style set** (A10): weaker identity; it still claims another lab in 9 of 52 thinking-ON answers.
- **Linear merges of A3 and A8a:** no blend gets both A3's BFCL and A8a's clean reasoning.

## Models

A3, A8a and A13 are archived in public HF repos under open-athena, with recipe, data hashes and scores in each card:

- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30`

spillover_issues.body: Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LVfMDHRBKBk_Bn9PY1J9Lb_MYwdUTFP5PkX2br25TNg/edit?tab=t.izhzsywzorld. Final results and the full ledger: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920#issuecomment-6076348127 (ledger also at https://gist.github.com/karansag/0ce1a07580bd430bc8c5b890069385b0). ## TL;DR (final, 2026-10-09). ** Given **one expert E** ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`)) built from the Snowball student B ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92 @ fdc3c3c5](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab)) by SFT on [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces, three methods were used to transfer E's gain back into B: * plain SFT on E's traces * SFT on rejection-sampled E traces (RS-SFT) * on-policy distillation from E (OPD). All three recover most or all of E's CruxEval gain on the 1,600 training-is-test prompts (4x sample traces from the test set size). Two-pass CruxEval input / output accuracy on the selected checkpoints: plain SFT 73.9 / 72.0, RS-SFT 80.8 / 77.9, OPD 79.6 / 75.2, against E 79.4 / 71.4 and B 55.4 / 57.8. RS-SFT and OPD are both 3–7 pp above plain SFT; the RS-SFT vs OPD ordering (1.2 / 2.7 pp) is unresolved with one run per arm and two evaluator passes. No arm dropped below B on GSM8K or MATH500. Training cost: plain SFT 61.6 H100-h, RS-SFT 57.4, OPD 376.4 for the full run (286.9 to the selected checkpoint, plus 14–15 per HF export). RS-SFT used ground-truth execution results to select demos; the other arms did not. These numbers measure transfer on seen prompts, not generalization. ## Results (selected checkpoints; CruxEval two-pass means, pass@1 %, 800 problems per direction; "gap closed" = gain over B divided by E's gain over B).** | Model | CruxEval input | CruxEval output | Gap closed (in / out) | GSM8K | MATH500 | Training H100-h | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | B ([baseline Snowball student, HF @ fdc3c3c5](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab)) | 55.4 | 57.8 | 0 | 90.4 | 89.8 | — | | [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) (teacher of E; served as `glm-5.3` through the internal glm53 relay, reasoning effort high) | 94.0 | 90.5 | — | — | — | — | | E (expert; B + SFT on GLM traces, step 272; [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`)) | 79.4 | 71.4 | 100% | 92.1 | 92.2 | 35.9 | | Plain SFT on E demos, 400 updates (final; [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399 @ 3e34be3f](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399/tree/3e34be3f884ff737f85354b060ea831ce0c90636) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-plain-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-399`)) | 73.9 | 72.0 | 77% / 104% | 94.0 | 92.6 | 61.6 | | RS-SFT on execution-correct E demos, 283 of 376 updates ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282 @ 073d128c](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282/tree/073d128cb1e53652126cce37a7cc2c96625d3c80) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-rs-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-282`)) | 80.8 | 77.9 | 106% / 148% | 93.5 | 93.6 | 57.4 (full run) | | OPD from E, 75 of 100 updates ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75 @ 9d189320](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75/tree/9d1893207226cf72f701187e1d5260d9fc3c931d) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/karan/skyrl/snowball-opd-cruxeval-e-2/exports/global_step_75/policy`)) | 79.6 | 75.2 | 101% / 128% | 92.5 | 90.4 | 286.9 to the checkpoint; 376.4 full run; +14–15 per HF export | ## Models Student B = [`open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92` @ `fdc3c3c5`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab) (Hugging Face commit; the repo received a later commit on 2026-10-13, so the pin matters). E = B after full SFT on 1,454 execution-correct [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces (trace collection: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/scratch/karan/glm-bench-traces/`) (LR 1e-5, 3 epochs, 272 updates, 32 H100, fresh optimizer state, frozen router biases), export [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`). E keeps B's tokenizer and chat template. E+ (E + 2 epochs at LR 1e-6; 80.2 / 75.1) was built as a separate reference and is not an arm. Every arm starts from B. ## Benchmark CruxEval (800 Python functions; input prediction and output prediction scored separately by executing the assertion). MATH500 was dropped as the target because B already scores 89.8% there; GSM8K and MATH500 are the collapse checks. Teacher gate: B 55.4 / 57.8; GLM 5.3 on the identical 1,600 prompts 94.0 / 90.5; E 79.4 / 71.4 (two-pass mean), passing the gate of B + 10 points on both tasks with no GSM8K drop. ## Frozen evaluator Marin `experiments.evaluation.cli launch` with Evalchemy [`ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8), vLLM on H100x8 (DP8 + EP8), `max_model_len` 32768, `max_gen_toks` 30720, `enable_thinking: true`, reasoning parser `grug`. Configs and pitfalls: https://gist.github.com/karansag/49de943771b98a7a23d9348b58933f71. Evalchemy's chat client sends no temperature, top_p or seed, and B's `generation_config.json` sets none, so every run samples at vLLM's default (temperature 1.0, unseeded). One pass on 800 problems has a binomial 95% half-width of about 3.5 pp; selected checkpoints get two passes. **Arms as run (all from B; AdamW LR 1e-6 constant, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, grad clip 1.0, router bias frozen; 4 epochs over the 1,600 prompts; one checkpoint per epoch).** - E demos: 8 samples per prompt from E at temperature 1.0, both directions, execution-graded in an isolated container (12,800 samples, 14.6 H100-h, shared by both SFT arms). - Plain SFT: E's first sample per prompt, correct or not (1,600 rows; 1.45M supervised tokens per epoch; batch 16; Levanter, 32 H100). - RS-SFT: first execution-correct sample per prompt (1,503 rows; 97 prompts with no correct sample stay in the eval denominator; 1.06M supervised tokens per epoch; Levanter, 32 H100). - OPD: [MarinSkyRL](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL), 4 on-policy rollouts per prompt at temperature 1.0, E as the teacher (sampled reverse KL on chosen tokens, no verifier), 64 prompts per update, 25 updates per epoch; 4 learner + 1 rollout + 1 teacher H100x8 nodes (Megatron). - Selection: the final checkpoint when it is similar or better than the previous one on both CruxEval directions, otherwise a second pass on both and the two-pass means decide. Plain SFT selected its final checkpoint (400 updates); RS-SFT (283 of 376) and OPD (75 of 100) selected their epoch-3 checkpoints after their finals dropped on one direction. ## Artifacts Trace browser (GLM, E, E+ traces, side-by-side compare): https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/072c90b0-281e-4692-a4bf-845874c021b1/. OPD W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/skyrl/runs/p3ie2bg7. Selected exports: plain [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399 @ 3e34be3f](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399/tree/3e34be3f884ff737f85354b060ea831ce0c90636) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-plain-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-399`), RS-SFT [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282 @ 073d128c](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282/tree/073d128cb1e53652126cce37a7cc2c96625d3c80) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-rs-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-282`), OPD [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75 @ 9d189320](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75/tree/9d1893207226cf72f701187e1d5260d9fc3c931d) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/karan/skyrl/snowball-opd-cruxeval-e-2/exports/global_step_75/policy`). Eval records: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals//record.json` (every record id is in the final comment's ledger). GPU-hour method: https://gist.github.com/karansag/500604143668730f8e79277b43f39298. ## Not in scope Weight merging (needs RL-trained experts that share B's init; none exist) and transfer from the older Snowball experts (none beats B under the matched eval). ## Decision log - 2026-10-06: matched eval of B and the existing experts (E6, E17a, E18, SWE, Stage-3) on MATH500/GSM8K; none beats B, so no promotion to teacher. - 2026-10-07: MATH500 near ceiling for B → CruxEval chosen; MMLU-Pro (B 44.1) and GPQA-D (B 41.9) measured as fallbacks and not used. - 2026-10-07: full SFT over LoRA for building E; LoRA kept as the fallback if full SFT collapses out-of-domain. - 2026-10-07: rejection-sampled SFT added as a third arm. - 2026-10-08: E frozen at step 272 for every arm; E+ built as a separate reference only. Arms changed from the plan: one sample per prompt for both SFT arms (not up to 4), no LR sweep, 4 rollouts per prompt for OPD. The arms ran in parallel on Iris. - 2026-10-09: RS-SFT and OPD final checkpoints not selected (drops on one direction with paired CI excluding 0); epoch-3 checkpoints selected on two-pass means. 🤖
# Research

Teacher training and three transfer arms make this a gated experiment. As of 23:29 UTC, the owner has submitted the W&B-corrected teacher retry; startup, optimizer progress, and export remain unconfirmed ([latest status](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920#issuecomment-6048938002)). No open PR targets #9920, while the owner is already preparing the recipe on `task/133`; the earlier coding-teacher spike [#9528](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9528) ended without a usable MOPD transfer result.

**Relevant code**
- [`experiments/sft/launcher.py#L494`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/sft/launcher.py#L494) — shared SFT specification and training setup
- [`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150) — versioned SkyRL experiment and export contract
- [`experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147) — shared evaluation launch path

# Proposed Fix

1. Follow the submitted teacher retry through a completed update, full training, and verified HF exports. Evaluate the planned exports with the frozen CruxEval/GSM8K configuration. Stop the transfer arms unless E clears the stated +10-point gate on both CruxEval directions without a GSM8K drop beyond noise.
2. Pin E, B, prompt IDs, tokenizer/template, grader, evaluator, and one eight-sample-per-prompt teacher generation artifact. Build unfiltered SFT from samples 1–4 and rejection-sampled SFT from up to four execution-correct samples. Record missing-correct-sample prompts, actual supervised tokens, and teacher-generation GPU-hours; a matched prompt set alone does not equalize training tokens.
3. Start OPD from the same B and prompts. Check teacher/student token-score alignment and one update plus export before the full run. Match the planned sweep and student update budget across arms, and record teacher-scoring GPU-hours separately.
4. Evaluate every selected arm twice with the same pinned evaluator on CruxEval input, CruxEval output, and GSM8K. Report each arm's accuracy, `(arm − B) / (E − B)` per direction, run-to-run spread, prompts and tokens consumed, and total GPU-hours. Label gains as transfer on the trained test prompts; this protocol cannot establish held-out generalization.
